title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 79-82): Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'structure' M, a set of elements X with a symmetric separation (disjointness) relation X ∥ Y. For A ⊂ M he defines cosupp A (essentially the elements separated from all of A, i.e. an orthogonal complement A^⊥) and supp A (essentially A^⊥⊥). ΣM is the poset of saturated subsets A = supp A. A 'support function' X ↦ |X| ⊂ P into the subsets of a set P is studied.

The Proposition on p. 80 assumes two conditions. Supp1: X ∥ Y iff |X| ∩ |Y| = ∅. Supp2: every singleton {x} is some |X|. Setting |A| = ⋃_{X∈A} |X|, it gives:
- |A| = |supp A|;
- |cosupp A| = P \ |A|;
- supp A ⊂ supp B iff |A| ⊂ |B|;
- A ∥ B iff |A| ∩ |B| = ∅;
- ΣM → 𝔓(P), A ↦ |A|, is an isomorphism of ordered sets compatible with the complement operation.
In modern terms, the closure lattice of an orthogonality space is a complete atomic Boolean algebra 𝔓(P) once such a separating, point-realising support exists.

Page 81 opens with an NB: these data determine P and A ↦ |A| up to canonical isomorphism, since P is recovered as the atoms of ΣM. Grothendieck presumes his other axioms ((ii_n), (iv_n), (v_n), or 'A1 2 2') then hold automatically.

He then leaves the 'quasi-ensembliste' (set-like) case for a geometric one. Start from a topological space P and take as 'liens' (links) L the compact contractible subsets of P. From these, build 'quasi-simplexes' of suitable bounded dimension (e.g. ≤ 1) by ad hoc conditions generalising the definition of a 'ficelle' (string). For dimension ≤ 1 he says he already gave a fully explicit definition. |X| is then defined in the obvious way, and 'tout marche' (everything works).

The caveat: if one keeps only the links traced on a given ficelle, the condition S_{VV_P} 2 (support compatible with the lattice operations) fails in general.

Example: the 'ficelle à deux brins', two arcs from 0 to 1, i.e. a circle with two marked points. The relevant links are the 'sections' cutting both strands at interior points x and x'. They are parametrised by I° = ]0,1[ × ]0,1[, with |z| = {x, x'}. The margin warns that here X ↦ |X| does not satisfy S_{VV_P} 1.

Page 82 completes the example for a product I × I' of two totally ordered sets with product order. For incomparable z1, z2, the support of a meet is strictly smaller than the intersection of supports: |B_{z1} ∩ B_{z2}| ⊊ |B_{z1}| ∩ |B_{z2}|. Dually, |A_{z1} ∨ A_{z2}| = [x1, x2] ∪ [x'2, x'1] strictly contains the four points. So the structure of sections of a non-simple string is not quasi-ensembliste: the order is only partial, and supports do not commute with lattice operations.

Purpose: find a combinatorial/axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame-topology-like foundations). Spaces would be recovered from abstract structures of pieces with a disjointness relation and support maps, and one tests which axioms survive for geometric models such as strings and compact contractible cells.
errors: 'Tout marche!' is asserted without proof for the general topological case. Even with compact contractible subsets as links, Supp2 needs points (singletons are compact contractible, fine), and the quasi-simplex axioms are explicitly left 'ad hoc'. The claim is a heuristic, not a verified statement.

The NB claim of uniqueness up to canonical isomorphism is plausible: P is recovered as the atoms of ΣM via Supp2. The claim that the remaining axioms hold 'automatically' is only presumed ('Je présume'), not checked.
No mathematical error in the two-strand example. The failure of the support to commute with meets is correctly diagnosed on p. 82 from the non-total product order.

ideas.what: Recovery of a point-set P and power-set lattice from an abstract structure with a disjointness relation and a support map; ΣM ≅ 𝔓(P) as ortho-ordered sets
ideas.modern_name: Closure lattice of an orthogonality space (A ↦ A^⊥⊥); representation of complete atomic Boolean algebras as power sets (Lindenbaum–Tarski)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lindenbaum–Tarski (atomic Boolean algebras); Dacey 1968, Foulis–Randall 1970s (orthogonality spaces)

ideas.what: Using compact contractible subsets ('liens') of a topological space as building blocks for 'quasi-simplexes' of bounded dimension, generalising 'ficelles' (strings)
ideas.modern_name: Cell/regular CW-like decompositions; tame-topology cell structures; 1-dimensional case close to graph/arc structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme (Esquisse d'un programme §5); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Spirit related to Esquisse d'un programme §5 ('topologie modérée'); the specific 'ficelle/lien' axiomatics not known to be published

ideas.what: Counterexample: on a two-strand string (circle with two marked points), sections form ]0,1[×]0,1[ with product order, and supports fail to commute with meets and joins
ideas.modern_name: Non-distributivity / non-Boolean behaviour of lattices of 'pieces' on a 1-dimensional complex; partially vs totally ordered cuts

missed.claim: Grothendieck's separation-relation structures with supp = double cosupport are orthogonality spaces in the sense of Dacey/Foulis–Randall. His Proposition is a spatial representation criterion for their closure ortholattice. The notes show no awareness of this quantum-logic literature, and conversely that literature does not link to his analysis situs project.
missed.quote: Ceci détermine P et l'application A → |A| à iso can. près.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could situate the 1986 analysis-situs axiomatics within the theory of orthogonality spaces and point-free topology. It might also suggest which of his axioms correspond to orthomodularity or Booleanity.

missed.claim: A programme to build 'quasi-simplexes' of arbitrary bounded dimension from compact contractible 'liens' in a topological space, generalising his explicit 1-dimensional 'ficelle' definition, is announced but only sketched ('conditions ad hoc').
missed.quote: On construit des "quasi-simplexes" convenables de dimension convenable, majorée, (p. ex. par 1) par des conditions ad hoc, généralisant celles qui définissent une ficelle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, unpublished attempt at the axiomatic tame topology of the Esquisse. It is comparable to o-minimal and stratified approaches, but based on contractible pieces and disjointness, and it remains undeveloped.

deep.surprise_reason: Interesting unpublished glimpse of Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic analysis situs (liens, ficelles, quasi-simplexes). The mathematics on the page is elementary: a power-set representation and a simple counterexample. The broader programme is known in spirit from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: 'comme un des parties compactes contractiles' should read roughly 'comme ensemble des parties compactes contractiles dans P'.
'p. ex. par 1) par des conditions' should read '(p. ex. par 1)) par des conditions'.
The condition named in the main text is likely 'S_{VV_P} 2' (matching the margin's 'S_{VV_P} 1'), not 'L_{VV_P} 2'.
'(en dehors x des 0,1)' is better read as '(un dehors de 0,1)', a parenthetical under the figure. The following line likely reads 'dont les liens seraient les "sections" de l'un et de l'autre brin'.
Margin reads approximately: 'Attention, ici, X ↦ |X| la fonction ne satisfait pas S_{VV_P} 1'.
'et si la fonction [?] ci-dessus' is more likely 'et si la fonction |·| [est] ci-dessus'; hard to read.
The final line ends with the ensemble produit I° = ]0,1[ × ]0,1[ followed by a period.
